514: The user interface provides consistent and role-appropriate interaction across the kiosk, staff panels, public display, and administrative modules. The system supports Cashier, Registrar, ITM, and Admission as separate service departments. The Head Admin can oversee all departments, while each Department Admin works within the assigned department. Clear controls, readable queue information, and synchronized status updates support Regular and Priority ticket processing.
522: The Student Number Input Screen allows a student to enter an identifier for record lookup or continue as a guest. Validated student information is used where required for service routing, including Registrar program-based window assignment. The Back to Welcome control returns the client to the starting screen.
527: The Service Selection Screen presents the enabled service departments: Cashier, Registrar, ITM, and Admission. After identifying as a student or guest, the client chooses the appropriate department and continues to its transaction and ticket-type workflow. Department availability follows the configured system settings.
531: The Registrar Queue Type Selection Screen displays the validated student name, academic program, and assigned Registrar window before presenting Regular and Priority options. In the illustrated example, a BSPSYCH student is assigned to Window 9. Priority is intended for eligible clients, including persons with disabilities, senior citizens, and pregnant clients, and requires security authorization before ticket generation. Regular selection proceeds through the standard ticket workflow.
535: The Login Interface authenticates authorized staff and administrators using their credentials. Cashier, Registrar, ITM, and Admission staff are directed to their operational workspace. The Head Admin receives system-wide access, while the four Department Admins receive access scoped to their assigned department.
542: The Cashier Panel in its ready state displays the assigned service window, current waiting count, and department waiting list. Call Next Ticket selects the next eligible Regular or Priority ticket using the system queue rules. Cashier staff process their own department queue rather than relying on ITM backup personnel.
546: The Cashier Panel in its serving state displays the active ticket and service timing information. Staff can complete the transaction or skip an unattended client, while the remaining waiting queue stays visible. These actions update ticket status and the recorded service history.
550: The Registrar Panel in its ready state displays the assigned Registrar window and its waiting Regular and Priority tickets. Each Registrar window processes tickets routed to that window. Open and Close controls update window availability so the kiosk and monitoring interfaces reflect the service point status.
554: The Registrar Panel in its serving state displays the current ticket, assigned window, and service controls. Completing or skipping the ticket updates the stored queue and transaction records and the synchronized staff and display interfaces. Recorded timestamps also support performance analysis and reporting.
564: The ITM Staff Panel is a dedicated interface for the ITM department. It displays ITM waiting tickets, the assigned ITM window, and the current service transaction. ITM staff call the next eligible Regular or Priority ticket, complete service, or skip an unattended client. ITM operates independently of Cashier, Registrar, and Admission and is not described as a backup-staff role.
568: The Staff Mini View provides a compact operational workspace for Cashier, Registrar, ITM, and Admission staff. It retains the logged-in staff identity, assigned window, waiting queue, current ticket, and permitted service actions. Registrar availability controls remain available in the supported Registrar view.
571: The Registrar Window Selection Screen allows the client to choose the Registrar window associated with the relevant academic program. Window 9 lists BSCRIM and BSPSYCH; Window 10 lists BSIT, BSCS, BSIE, and BSCPE; Window 11 lists BSHM and BSTM; Window 12 lists BSA and EDUC/PTCP; and Window 13 lists BSBA. This screen supports the manual selection workflow, while identified students can receive a program-based assignment.
576: The Security Authorization Screen requests a valid security code for an eligible Priority request. The system validates the code before allowing the Priority ticket workflow to continue. Regular ticket requests do not require this priority authorization.
579: The Generated Queue Ticket Confirmation Screen displays the issued ticket number and service information after the kiosk workflow is completed. The saved ticket becomes available to the appropriate department queue. The kiosk sends a signed receipt to the local thermal printing service, and ticket details remain visible if printing is unavailable.
584: The Admin Dashboard presents queue and service-performance indicators using recorded system data. The Head Admin can monitor Cashier, Registrar, ITM, and Admission, while Department Admins see information within their assigned department. Operational summaries and intelligence panels support review of waiting queues, service activity, and departmental performance.
591: The Queue Monitoring Interface displays service-window availability, assigned staff, current tickets, and waiting counts. The Head Admin can review all enabled departments; Department Admins are restricted to their assigned department. The screen supports operational supervision without changing the independent Cashier, Registrar, ITM, and Admission staff workflows.
597: The Analytics Interface displays recorded queue volume, transaction trends, waiting and service times, completion rates, and service-window performance for the permitted department and selected period. Filters allow administrators to review relevant data, while department-based access restrictions define the scope of the displayed results.
602: The Reports Interface summarizes queue and service records for the selected period and permitted department. KPI cards, charts, and staff or window summaries use the reporting dataset returned by the application. PDF export refreshes the selected report data before generating a downloadable report for administrative review.
607: The Staff Management Interface displays staff and Department Admin accounts, including their names, roles, departments, assigned windows, and account status. The Head Admin manages accounts across the system, including the four Department Admin roles. Department Admins manage permitted staff accounts and assignments within their own departments.
610: The Display Board Settings Interface allows the Head Admin to configure enabled departments, service-window presentation, labels, colors, branding, media, and announcements. A preview supports checking the display before publishing. Published settings are used by the public queue display and relevant department-availability controls.
614: The Activity Logs Interface presents recorded access and queue-processing events with staff identity, department, assigned window, action, and timestamp. Search and history controls support reviewing calls, completions, skipped tickets, and other recorded operational events for accountability.
619: The Queue Display Board shows currently served tickets and their assigned service windows, together with department waiting information. Its layout follows the enabled-department and display settings. Audio announcements identify called tickets and service points, helping clients proceed to the correct window.
